newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil backwardation to widen after expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil backwardation to widen after expiry.

text.p: Steep backwardation in the IPE gas oil market will continue even after the spot September contract expires on Thursday, as the oil industry braces for winter with lean inventories and pent up demand, analysts and traders said.
They were bullish on the spreads while at the same time were reluctant to pick any price objectives on an outright basis.
In late afternoon trading Monday, Sept slid $3.25 to $216.50 a tonne and Oct was off $2.50 at $208, leaving the spread at $8.50.
The spread blew out from a $1.50 backwardation on August 27 to a close of $9.25 a tonne on Friday, and traders said the spread was trading at even wider levels during that session.
The Oct/Nov spread, based on the outright prices, was at a $5.75 backwardation and was expected to move out toward at least $9-$10, maybe $15, during the month, some said.
"In my view I see that spread still very strong," said one European distillates trader.

"I would imagine that we are going to be with backwardation through toward the end of the first quarter," he said. "I don't see any relief in the backwardation until then...From all I can see, the gas oil market is in very short supply."
The wide backwardation on the IPE was expected to continue even though the three nearby heating oil contracts on the NYMEX were trading almost at parity.
"The situation in the States is also very tight but I don't think they have the same draw this time of year that goes on in Germany," the trader said.
"In particular (demand) in inland Germany has been pushed further down the calendar because of the strong oil price and because of the strong dollar and that has kept the Germans out."

As of end-July, middle distillate supplies in Europe were 282.53 million barrels, down 10.49 million from a year ago, according to Euroilstock data. In Germany, inventories stood at 88.13 million, down slightly from 89.59 million in July 1995.

"I would have thought it was less likely to go out further but obviously what we're seeing in the expiring September is a warning shot that the market is emotional and vulnerable very much to shifting perceptions," said Charles Gray at Prudential.
"The way we're seeing this October moving up to $212 it's constructive and to me it looks like, all things being equal, it can go higher," he said.
October gas oil hit a new contract high earlier at $212.50. September reached $221.75, a contract high and strongest level in nearly five years.

"I would tend to feel there is a good base in these spreads at the moment and in due course October/November could approach the numbers September/October was trading," said Tim Holmes at MeesPierson Derivatives. "I wouldn't fight it."
